subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Light Roast: Origin Forward
description: A quick, practical guide to Light Roast: Origin Forward.

hook.text: Light roasts are pulled at or shortly after first crack. They preserve the bean's origin character above all else.

buildup.text: Flavors lean toward fruit, floral, citrus, and tea-like notes. Acidity is high. Body is lighter. Color is cinnamon to tan.

discovery.text: Light roasting requires exceptional green coffee—there's nowhere for defects to hide when the roast barely masks anything.

twist.text: Many people find light roasts too acidic or 'sour' if they're used to dark roast. It's an acquired preference.

climax.text: The specialty coffee movement champions light roasts. They let terroir and processing speak louder than the roaster's hand.

punchline.text: Light roast: the bean talks. The roaster listens.

quiz.question: Why does light roasting require high-quality green coffee?
options: There's nowhere for defects to hide when the roast barely masks anything
